detect_code_similarity.py.summary: Detect the identical and similar Python files of a tree.
details: Normalizes each file (comments and formatting dropped), hashes it, compares the pairs with difflib and optionally ssdeep/tlsh, and writes a JSON report of the exact duplicates and of the pairs above the similarity threshold (70 % by default).

detect_empty_pkgs.py.summary: Find the empty or useless Python archives (tar.gz, wheel, zip).
details: Opens each archive of the current directory and flags the ones without code (no files, only metadata, only ``setup.py``, only ``__pycache__``, only docs/tests, import-only modules or trivially small content), moving them into ``./empty`` with ``-a``.

detect_noneng.py.summary: Detect the Chinese, Persian, Japanese and Korean text in files.
details: Matches the CJK, kana, hangul and Arabic script ranges in the files below a directory (10 MB limit), reports the hits and with ``-c`` copies each file into ``~/tmp/langs/<lang>``; it is a dry run by default.

detect_nonenglish.py.summary: Find the non-English content of text files with a chosen language-detection backend.
details: ``--backend`` picks gcld3, pycld2, langdetect, lingua or fast-langdetect, the files are filtered by extension, excluded directories and size, and the result goes to a text or JSON report (``-l`` adds the per-line findings) with a confidence threshold.

dhtools.py.summary: Toolbox for the local ``dh`` package: reverse, inline and usage report.
details: Subcommands: ``reverse`` replaces the locally copied ``dh`` functions with ``from dh import ...`` (``-a`` writes, the default is a dry run), ``inline`` pastes the imported sources back into the files and ``usage`` scans a script folder and reports which ``dh`` helpers it uses. ``--match`` and ``--import-style`` choose how the functions are recognised and imported.

dirinfo.py.summary: Report the file types and sizes of a directory.
details: Scans the given path, groups the files by extension with their counts and sizes, prints the report (``-s`` saves it to ``/sdcard/.dirinfo``) and ``-i`` renders the same data as a Matplotlib bar chart in English or Persian.

dirsizes.py.summary: Find the files and directories with the largest footprint.
details: Walks a directory with a bounded depth, keeps the top K entries by recursive size (or by the individual file size with ``--mode file``), honours the ``--exclude`` patterns and prints a rich table, optionally reversed.

dirtools.py.summary: Unified directory analysis and folderization toolkit.
details: Subcommands: ``info``/``subdirs`` print the size report and the charts, ``list``/``tree`` show the entries, and ``split-range``/``split-count``/``split-greedy``/``split-even`` move the files into folders by size range, by count or max size, by greedy bin packing or by an even split.

dirz.py.summary: List the top-level directories of the current directory, optionally with their sizes.
details: Prints the subdirectories one per line and, with the size flag, the recursive total of each of them in a sorted, human-readable listing.

dl.py.summary: Unified downloader with wget, check and size subcommands.
details: Subcommands: ``wget`` downloads the URLs of a list (or the one given) with urllib, requests or pycurl, ``check`` tests whether the links are alive and ``size`` prints the remote sizes without downloading; ``--download-small`` fetches the files under the size limit, ``--filter-ext`` restricts the extension and ``--update-file`` rewrites the list with only the failed URLs.

Subcommands: ``chat-export`` turns a JSON conversation list into per-chat Markdown, ``info-to-md`` shells out to the ``info`` reader, ``man-to-md`` renders a roff page, ``md-to-html`` writes styled HTML with Tailwind and KaTeX, ``rst-to-html`` goes through docutils, ``mobi-to-html`` extracts a ``.mobi``, ``pptx-to-txt`` pulls the slide text and ``rst-to-md`` uses pandoc.

dostring_browser.py.summary: Browse the module docstrings of a directory in a paged Markdown view.
details: Extracts the docstring of each ``.py`` file with ast, renders the documents with rich and pages through them with the space/arrow keys, ``n``/``p`` for the next or previous file and ``q`` to quit.

drmc.py.summary: Strip the comments, docstrings and annotations of Python files.
details: ``-c`` removes the comments, ``-d`` the docstrings, ``-a``/``-x`` everything, ``-t`` the annotations; the backend is ast, LibCST or tree-sitter (``-b``), the writes are atomic, and ``--dry-run``, ``--diff``, ``--backup`` and every pool method are available.

dt1.py.summary: Translate a text file in resumable chunks.
details: Splits the text into ~2500-character chunks, translates them with DeepL, deep_translator, translate, Bing, googletrans or pygoogletranslation (automatic fallback), saves the ``chunks.json`` progress periodically, throttles the requests and lists the failed chunk indexes.

dt2.py.summary: Translate the lines of a text file with progress saving.
details: Groups the lines into chunks of 2000 characters, translates them with ``deep_translator`` in parallel, saves the progress every ten chunks and on interruption, and writes plain text, JSON or merged source/translation pairs (``-o``).

dt3.py.summary: Translate a text file in independently resumable chunks with many backends.
details: Supports DeepL, deep_translator, translate, Bing, googletrans, pygoogletranslation, boto3, Azure, Baidu, Alibaba and Watson, maps the language codes per backend, atomically saves the chunk results, skips the identity translations and logs to a rotating file.
dt3.py.usage: dt3 -i input.txt -o out.json [-s auto] [-t en] [-b BACKEND]
